# ON PHYSIOLOGY, CHAPTER I.

->...meanwhile, the opinion remains that the Sun is the Father, the Earth indeed is the Mother only of our Beings, the Moon is the nurse, and the Stars are the handmaidens <note>original: "pedissequæ"; female attendants or servants</note>, until we attain other uses. Now let us return to the account of the constitution already begun.<-

The Moon, because it was nearest to the Earth, was deprived of much heat and pure light. It retains certain darkish spots which it received during the conflict <note>Referring to the primordial struggle between the principles of Heat and Cold</note> when smoke exhaled from the mass and was converted into the heaven and stars—unless it be a "system" <note>original: "systema"; Campanella uses this term to suggest a complex world-structure like Earth, containing various elements, rather than a pure celestial body of fire.</note>. Thus, in the Moon, matter could not be well purified; it remained like a cloud and devoid of manifest light. Hence, half of it is perpetually illuminated by the Sun; but sometimes it appears full when it is opposite to the Sun and we are in the middle. Sometimes nothing shines for us when it moves with the Sun, and its side opposite to us is illuminated. And it often covers the face of the Sun for us because it is impure; nor does it allow the sun’s light to leap across to us through its body, which is called an eclipse <term>eclipsatio</term>. Just as the shadow of the earth sometimes hinders the Sun's light and darkens the full moon across its diameter.

At other times it appears half-full, sometimes more or less, according to whether it is more or less distant from the Sun and our eyes are between them. This variety of the Moon was most useful, according to the divine counsel, for the diversity of lower things and so that the Earth might not be consumed <note>Campanella suggests the Moon acts as a buffer or regulator, preventing the Sun's intense heat from destroying life on Earth.</note>.

<margin>
b. From here are resolved the arguments of Aristotle and others who think the heaven is not...
</margin>

The other Planets indeed did not receive as much heat as would equal the higher stars: because they were made nearer to the contrary <note>The "contrary" refers to the Earth, the center of coldness.</note>. And divine wisdom provided thus, lest the Earth be destroyed <gloss>b</gloss> by them and the worldly statue <note>original: "mundana statua"; a metaphor for the physical structure or fabric of the universe viewed as a masterpiece of divine art.</note> collapse; which is not caused by the higher stars, since they are too distant from it.

<sig>B 2</sig>
<meta>catchword: But the opinion that the heaven is not</meta>

*...fiery, because it would destroy the Earth, as is clear in the text. Regarding the other argument saying that the Heaven is moved by circular motion, while fire moves in a straight line, and therefore the heaven is not fiery: I respond by saying that motion is not contrary to motion, but to rest. Therefore there are two elements: one mobile [heat/fire], the other immobile [cold/earth]. And since the nature of fire is mobile, and it can neither go further upward nor downward toward its enemy [the cold], it is necessary that it be moved in a circle; while the earth stands still once it has arrived at its own totality <term>vniuersitas</term>. And the natures of things are to be considered within these totalities, and not outside of them.*

<summary>Campanella explains the Moon's composition as "impure" and cloud-like, which accounts for its phases and eclipses. He further argues against Aristotle, claiming the heavens are indeed made of fire/heat, but their distance and circular motion preserve the Earth from destruction.</summary>

But neither now, nor ever, will the Sun and the Planets, and the earth, and whatever is contained in the universal statue <note>original: "statua vniuersali"; Campanella views the universe as a grand, living monument or statue crafted by God.</note>, change their path, course, and being, until every Being has been changed into every other Being—as now appears in the irregularities—and the whole shall be consumed into the good intended by the First Wisdom, the world having been purified by fire.

It is a thing marvelous to consider.

### On Divine Providence, whose Instruments are Necessity, Fate, and Harmony.

#### ARTICLE II.

<margin>a. There is a wonderful providence in the preservation of the World without force; whatever happens, happens for the better.</margin>
<margin>b. Two contraries equally robust in action cannot produce a third thing: and therefore no mixture is given.</margin>

If indeed the Earth had stood outside the heaven, or if it had been necessary to flee from an enemy, the World would not have obtained the beautiful distinction which the two primary bodies <note>Heat (associated with the Sun/Heavens) and Cold (associated with the Earth).</note> create. Or, if it had been unable to flee, it would have remained burnt on the side where the fiery globe invaded, and remained frozen on the other side where the less robust contrary [Cold] fled and gathered itself. Therefore, the beautiful Beings <note>original: "Entia" – referring to all created things like plants, animals, and minerals.</note> that now exist would not have come to be: for the contrary cold would necessarily have had to yield and be extinguished, or <margin>b</margin> stand with equal forces, in which case no third Being could have been formed. But since it remained in the middle of its contrary, now conquering and now being conquered in turn, it happens that secondary Beings are made without the destruction of the less robust contrary. For as the heaven circles the earth itself, its thin and weak parts cannot conquer; nor indeed can the gathered and strong parts, because they are sufficiently distant and continuously change their position, and for the other reasons mentioned. # F. THOMAS CAMPANELLA

Present light creates day: however, darkness extended into a *d* pyramid from the base of the earth [because the Sun far exceeds it in size] creates night. And perpetually night and day, evening and morning occur on the earth as the victorious light circles around, while darkness reigns in the opposite part and follows behind. Therefore, *e* just as in its revolution from east to west it creates two main cycles, Day and Night, in 24 hours: so also in its transition from tropic to tropic at the same time it creates Summer and Winter, the former corresponding to day, and the latter to night. For where the Sun is nearest and directly overhead, its light leaping upon the earth bounces back *f* united, collected, multiplied, and increased; therefore it creates excessive heat, which is called Summer. But where it hangs oblique and remote, cold prevails, making winter. Thus, when it is Day or Summer in some location on earth; in the *g* opposite place it is Night and Winter, although this truly occurs under the opposite horizontal pole. In certain regions, specifically under the Equator, they always have twelve hours of day and twelve hours of night: because the circle of vision of the inhabitants, which is called the Horizon, is bounded at the two poles, since they themselves reside in the middle of the stationary earth in the middle of heaven: and the Horizon itself divides all the parallel circles...

<margin>
*d* When a light-giving body is equal in size to an opaque one, the shadow extends in a cylindrical shape; when it is smaller or larger, it forms a pyramid. Its base is on the opaque body if the light is larger (as happens with the Earth and the Sun); if the light were smaller, the base would be at the end of the shadow and the cone would be on the opaque body.
</margin>

*e* Evening and morning are the borders of night and day: likewise Autumn and Spring for summer and winter. However, these are not the primary seasons corresponding to the elements. For those who live under the poles have day in place of summer, and night in place of winter.

# CHAPTER II OF THE PHYSIOLOGY

...circles, which are the 365 daily paths of the Sun, always into two equal parts. Thus, it <note>the Sun</note> remains for just as much time above the earth as beneath the earth in respect to those people <note>those living on the Equator</note>. In other regions, however, days and nights are always varying according to how they tilt from the Equator toward the poles; they increase or decrease according to the distance and proximity of the Sun and the tilt of their individual <term>Horizons</term> <note>the boundary where the sky meets the earth, which changes based on the observer's location</note>, which therefore cut the paths of the sun into unequal parts continually, until one reaches the land beneath the poles; where six of our months are a single day, and the other six a single night. For the Sun stays for six months on this side of the equator—three in traveling from it toward the <term>tropic</term> <note>the northern or southern limits of the sun's path</note>, and three in returning to the equator—during which time the inhabitants near the poles continually see the Sun itself circling above the Horizon, causing the shadows to circle likewise, because the Equator itself serves as their Horizon. Similarly, it is the opposite for the other inhabitants of the pole called Antarctic, which is opposite to ours called Arctic; which <margin>h Aristotle incorrectly placed the East on the right and the West on the left, but rather the opposite is held from Holy Scripture: although the reason assigned teaches that the North is the right side,</margin> *h* because it has more and brighter stars, it ought to be seen as the "right" side of the World, and the opposite as the "left." This cannot apply to the East and West, since the same vertical point is simultaneously East, West, and South when related to different locations on the earth at once.

<margin>Isaiah the Prophet <note>original: "I’ai. Prop b."; likely a reference to Isaiah 45:18, "He did not create it to be empty, but formed it to be inhabited."</note></margin>
Wisdom said that the whole Earth should be inhabited: therefore, beneath the Equator *i* there are happy dwellings for moderate beings, such as humans, which the perpetual equality of day and night creates. Under the tropics, however, because the Sun reaches them and then returns—and therefore stays for more time at once and doubles its strength—our beings there are half-scorched, arid, and their dwellings are reduced to ash. Toward the poles, however, outside the tropics, heat and cold occupy the dwellings to a greater or lesser degree according to their greater or lesser proximity to the path of the sun.

*& furthermore, the stay of the Sun is longer, etc. The man imagined by Aristotle, with his right hand in the East and his left in the West, is a fantasy; for the construction of the World is not taken from us, but ours from the World. Also, given that we walk well from the rising to the setting sun, reaching out our right hand to the north and our left to the south. Therefore, etc. i Aristotle and Virgil, wandering in error, denied there were habitations under the Equator and under the poles, although there light and shadow, in equal alternation, create a perpetual temperate climate. Under the poles, indeed, the long duration of light tempers the long duration of darkness. Avicenna <note>an influential Persian philosopher and physician</note> and Albertus Magnus <note>a 13th-century German scholar and saint</note> guessed more correctly, and in modern times, sailors experience this truth. ## *On Time.*

### ARTICLE III.

<margin>From the Epistle of St. James the Apostle. <note>Likely referring to James 1:17: "with whom there is no variation or shadow due to change."</note></margin>
<margin>a Aristotle, by saying that Time is the "measure of motion," did not define time itself, but its use among us—and even this he defined incorrectly, since time is also a measure of rest, and the solar motion is a measure of time more than time is a measure of the motion. But Aristotle was ignorant of what that <term>essence</term> <note>original: *quidditas*, or "what-ness"</note> of time is, which allows us to use it as a measure.</margin>
This succession of day and night, of heat and cold, of unity and multitude, of motion and rest, of change and stillness, is called **Time**. This becomes known to us through the most manifest movement of the Sun. The **First Mind** granted us this method of measuring things through the part of them most known to us. a Nevertheless, every measure, besides the fact that it exists as a measure, is something in itself: it just so happens that we use it in place of a measure; just as a "palm" <note>An ancient unit of length based on the hand's width</note>, besides being a measure for cloth, is in itself an outspread hand.

## On the Movements and Use of the Stars.

### C A P. III.

This indeed happened by necessity from the origin of things, according to the first plan: for it is not only one Sun—through the variety of its straight, daily motion of 24 hours, and its annual motion of 365 oblique circles, with certain minutes added as it moves from one <term>tropic</term> <note>The two latitudes (Cancer and Capricorn) representing the Sun's furthest limits north and south</note> to the other—that produces in matter a diversity corresponding to the degrees of the Primary Idea. # FRIAR TOMMASO CAMPANELLA

<margin>
b. Ptolemy <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century astronomer who established the geocentric model</note> marks the Equator and the tropics in the starry sky, but since descriptions of it vary, they must be fixed elsewhere. Nor does Copernicus think they are on the earth, for they vary there too. That the Zodiac is the path of the Sun and is unstable is demonstrated by the variation of the fixed stars in latitude, which is as great as the continuous inclination of the Zodiac toward the equator.
</margin>

In the immense space, *b* where the World is located, the equinoctial circle <note>The celestial equator</note> is designated in a position that divides the heaven into equal parts, and the earth likewise; yet it is found neither in the heaven nor in the earth <note>original: "at non in cælo neq; in terra"; likely meaning it is an abstract mathematical division rather than a physical object</note>. This circle is divided into 360 parts by human wisdom. The starry heaven indeed revolves in this space entirely every 24 hours, while in its description it displays 365 parts like the Galaxy <note>the Milky Way</note>; this heaven, composed of many little stars, can be seen to vary so that it might produce diversity on earth and provide a path for celestial lives. The extreme points upon which the heaven turns are called the poles. The line extended from pole to pole through the center of the earth is called the Axis. And the closer the parts of the heaven are to the poles, the slower they move; similarly, the closer they are to the center, because they describe a narrower circle. The same thing happens with the ideal and worldly celestial wheel as with all other wheels: they are faster at the circumference and the middle, but slower at the center and at the poles. Whether the entire <term>machine of the world</term> <gloss>original: "machina Mundi"; the universe viewed as a complex, functioning mechanism</gloss> moves along with its poles is unknown to our senses; yet certain irregularities <note>original: "exorbitantiæ"</note> show a kind of instability within the machine of the World, and perhaps in other systems outside our World that are unknown to us.

<margin>
c. The wandering stars <note>The planets</note> and the Sun are clearly seen to revolve upon themselves.
</margin>

*c* However, the more concentrated parts of the highest heaven—namely the stars themselves—rotate upon themselves, in addition to the motion they have with the whole. For since they are hotter and more vigorous, they cannot be seen as content with the common motion alone. This is especially true for the polar stars, whose low velocity does not satisfy their internal vigor; therefore, they all seem to twinkle <note>original: "scintillare"</note> and, as it were, to stagger. But the Planets, since they are closer to the earth and less vigorous, and are positioned within the tropics, appear content with the ordinary motion, without revolving upon themselves. This the Moon *d* teaches us, always showing us the same cloudy face and always in the same position; except for the Sun, which does not seem content with the common motion alone and revolves upon itself, because it is most abundant and robust—
<meta>catchword: —ly</meta>

---

Nor does their twinkling happen because of distance, as Aristotle and Copernicus wrote; for then Saturn would twinkle more than Mercury, but we experience the opposite. *d* Aristotle wrongly concludes from the fact that the Moon does not revolve upon itself that the fixed stars do not revolve either; for their strength differs from the weakness <note>original: "languore"</note> of the Moon. But he was deceived by his belief that the stars are carried by the heaven like <term>knots in a board</term> <gloss>A metaphor for the Aristotelian idea that stars are fixed rigidly into crystalline spheres like knots in a piece of wood</gloss>.

# ON PHYSIOLOGY, CHAPTER III.

...and has the most heat, as is clearly shown in reflections of water placed below at its rising and setting.

<margin>
*e* I wonder that Telesio <note>Bernardino Telesio (1509–1588), a natural philosopher who argued that heat and cold were the primary principles of nature. Campanella was heavily influenced by him but often critiqued his mechanics.</note> posited neither more spheres nor poles, since he made the heaven equal and very thin, making it impossible for it to be distinguished into separate spheres. Nor did he explain how simple fire could be cut into these spheres, nor how they could move obliquely without the physical slantedness of spheres and poles. But if such things were necessary, one would still have to posit eccentrics and epicycles <term>eccentrics and epicycles: mathematical circles used in ancient astronomy to explain why planets seem to speed up, slow down, or move backward</term>, which he remains silent about; therefore, the spheres themselves should have been passed over in silence.
</margin>

Under the starry *e* heaven, the planets are carried around—not dragged by the heaven, but moving by themselves, like birds in the air, since they are hotter than the heaven itself. Nor can the heaven be divided into different physical spheres such as would be required for the diversity of their motions, since the whole is uniform, continuous, and thin: so much so that it admits division far less than air or water, which, when divided, is immediately reunited. Saturn travels highest of all below the fixed stars; after him Jupiter, then Mars, then *f* Venus; beneath her is the Sun; Mercury follows him; but the last and nearest to us is the Moon. Therefore, being placed between them and us, she obscures not only the Sun, but all the planets and fixed stars from our view.

The motion of the stars is not as unstable, irregular, or haphazard as that of birds, because the stars do not seek food, nor comfortable regions, nor do they flee from troubles or hostile beings; nor are they driven in every direction by every whim of the imagination. In truth, over a long period of time, even their irregularity becomes manifest, which is nevertheless reduced to an eternal series, known in part to their own minds <note>Campanella believed that all things, including stars, possessed a degree of "sense" or consciousness.</note>.

They all move from East to West, along with the fixed stars; but they decline slightly, alternating to the North and to the South, and the extreme points of this declination are called the Northern and Southern tropics. The common middle point, from which they began to run out, is called the equinoctial <note>The celestial equator</note>. All such circles are marked in the immense space. However, the path of declination is not straight but oblique, and it is called the Zodiac, or the oblique circle, the path of the sun. But for the planets, this path has no specific name. And thus it is oblique, and

<sig>C 2</sig>
<meta>catchword: in</meta>

---

*...which he is silent about: therefore, the spheres also should have been left unmentioned. ¶ St. Chrysostom <note>A 4th-century Church Father</note> and Theodoret <note>A 5th-century theologian</note> posit a single heaven not cut into spheres, just as I do; though it is called "heavens" in the plural in the Hebrew language, just as "nuptials" <note>original: "nuptiae"</note> is plural in Latin. Add also the different regions, as we say "the world of lands" <note>original: "orbem terrarum"</note>. f We have assigned the Sun to the fifth place because Venus and Mercury are often seen at their apogee <term>apogee: the point in an orbit furthest from the Earth</term> above it; for which reason Timaeus <note>The main speaker in Plato's dialogue "Timaeus," representing Pythagorean cosmology</note>, whom Aristotle and Plato followed, gave the Sun the sixth place. Ptolemy, however, gave it the fourth, because those same planets seem closer to us at their perigee <term>perigee: the point in an orbit closest to the Earth</term> below the Sun. But both they and he do not seem to have considered correctly, because they observed them in different states. I, however, have placed Venus above the Sun because Venus is found to recede further from the Sun than Mercury. It also suits the Sun to have a retinue of perpetual companions surrounding him, rather than him alone standing by them.*

<summary>Campanella argues that the heaven is a single, thin medium rather than a series of solid spheres, and that planets move through it like sentient "birds" of fire. He proposes a specific planetary order, placing the Sun in the fifth position, and critiques previous astronomers like Ptolemy and Telesio.</summary>

<meta>This page continues Campanella's astronomical discussion. He is moving from the physical composition of the heavens to the specific mechanics of planetary motion, arguing against the Aristotelian idea that planets move in a contrary direction to the stars. Instead, he proposes they simply "lag behind" due to their distance from the source of motion.</meta>

<header>FRIAR THOMAS CAMPANELLA</header>

...divided into 360 degrees, because they do not circle around as quickly as the fixed stars, but are always left a little bit behind; otherwise, their path would be straight from one tropic to the other, and would cover only forty-seven degrees.

<margin>
*g* Nor does the mind grasp through imagination how the same celestial body can be carried by contrary motions at the same time, one of which is "violent" <note>In Aristotelian physics, "violent motion" is motion forced upon an object against its nature, while "natural motion" is its inherent tendency.</note> occurring in 24 hours, and the other natural—occurring in 29 days for the Moon and 30 years for Saturn—and how a body in which violence prevails over nature is not dissolved.
</margin>

*g* However, this is not a "leaving behind" of motion, but a lack of motion, and it should be called "sub-deficiency" <note>original: *subdeficientia*. This is Campanella's key argument: planets don't move backward (east to west); they just move forward more slowly than the stars, appearing to lose ground.</note>. Therefore, while the fixed stars complete 360 parts of the equator in the imaginary space of 24 hours, Saturn travels only 359 degrees and 58 minutes. Jupiter travels 359 degrees and 55 minutes. Mars travels 359 degrees and 29 minutes. But Venus, the Sun, and Mercury travel almost 359 degrees, since Venus and Mercury are satellites of the Sun himself, the Leader in the war against the Earth <note>Campanella often uses military metaphors for the elemental struggle between the Sun (Heat) and the Earth (Cold).</note>. Finally, the Moon travels almost 346 degrees and 57 minutes in its motion from east to west. Thus, the sub-deficiency of Saturn is two minutes; of Jupiter, about 5; of Mars, about 30; of Venus, the Sun, and Mercury, 59 minutes and nearly 8 seconds; and finally, of the Moon, almost 13 degrees and 3 minutes.

This was reasonable so that the closer they are to the starry Empyrean <term>Empyrean: the highest, most fire-filled part of heaven, thought to be the source of all heat and motion</term> heaven, the faster the vital motion they would obtain, and the more distant, the slower. Also, it was so they would not always run together but be separated from one another, joined, and gaze at each other through diameter, triangle, square, and hexagonal aspects <note>These refer to astrological "aspects" (opposition, trine, square, and sextile), which were believed to influence earthly events based on the geometric relationship between planets.</note> and other configurations. Thus, the Beings that are born and reborn on earth would vary, and the infinite participability of the First Idea would be received through modes...

---

...prevalence over nature. Therefore, we have removed "violent motion" from the heaven and restored "love" to the whole thing, which is moved by a single nature of heat, differing only in abundance and strength; thus it goes the same way, but some of its parts go faster, and some indeed slower. Contrary to reason, Aristotle thinks the celestial orbs are moved by angels <note>original: *intelligentiae*. Aristotle and the scholastics believed spiritual beings or "Intelligences" were required to physically push the planetary spheres.</note>; for not every motion occurs from a separate mover, as he asserts. For natural motions occur from an intrinsic form, whereas only violent motions occur from an extrinsic one. Scotus and Durandus <note>John Duns Scotus (c. 1266–1308) and Durand of Saint-Pourçain (c. 1275–1334), medieval theologians who questioned the necessity of angels as physical movers of the heavens.</note> recognized this regarding heavy and light things, as did Telesio and Seneca. Therefore, its own heat is sufficient to move the heaven, just as cold is for quieting the earth. 

Moreover, so that it may always be moved forward regularly, it does not need an angel, as Alexander of Aphrodisias <note>A famous 2nd-century commentator on Aristotle who argued for a more mechanized view of the universe.</note> thinks. But indeed, motion is a life-giving, conservative act of the heaven, not a "passion" <term>passion: in philosophy, "passion" refers to an object being acted upon by an external force, rather than the object acting of its own will</term>, as they think. Therefore it happens with pleasure, and always in the same way, unless it is disturbed from elsewhere. Just as the earth always rests in the same way. Nor do the elements labor while they move or rest, because motion and rest are neither action nor passion, but an operation following from existence itself, in which the mover and the moved are the same—which is not the case in external actions. 

Likewise, it is madness to think that Angels move the secondary orbs so that they might imitate God the first mover, since they are moved—according to their own testimony—"against" God, that is, from west to east. Therefore their action would be war and counter-action, not imitation. Also, if they who move the stars are blessed, those who must turn the resisting orbs (according to Aristotle) will be unhappy, because they never truly reach the end of their moving. Also, why do those who move toward the North yield the motion to the South to others? And how could they give up their own blessedness, which is supposedly found in motion? Does it never tire them?

<summary>Campanella argues that planets do not have "contrary" motions but simply lag behind the fixed stars (sub-deficiency) due to their internal heat. He rejects the Aristotelian idea that angels/intelligences are required to push the planetary spheres, asserting that motion is a natural, pleasurable expression of a body's own form.</summary>

### ON PHYSIOLOGICAL MATTERS, CHAPTER III. ###

...infinite ways, scattered and designated by the manifold variety of powers—acting and receiving, cooperating and reacting—and moderated according to the fated order prescribed by the **First Wisdom** <note>In Campanella’s philosophy, "First Wisdom" refers to God's divine design or the Primal Wisdom (*Primalitas Sapientia*), which governs the laws of nature.</note>.

The Moon makes the reason for this **sub-deficiency** <note>original: *subdeficientia*. As established on the previous page, this refers to the planet "falling short" of the speed of the fixed stars rather than moving in a contrary direction.</note> plain to see. For if this evening she is seen setting with the Sun beneath the western horizon, then on the following day, when the Sun is found at that same point on the horizon, she herself will be seen to be 12 degrees distant from him toward the east. On the day after that, she will be nearly 24 degrees away and more illuminated, though her horns point toward the east. This is because the Sun looks upon her from above and from the west, so that little of her illuminated half is granted to us, who look up at her underside from below. The horns, moreover, are extended by this oblique light. 

This "sub-deficiency" of the Moon relative to the Sun is not a movement from west to east—since nature always seems to be carried toward the west—but occurs because she is outrun by the Sun, just as a slow traveler is passed by a swifter one. Similarly, on the third day after, she is found nearly 37 degrees behind, as the degrees of the third day’s lag are added to those of the two preceding days. Thus, on the 7th day, she will be seen in the middle of the sky, 90 degrees distant from the Sun and half-full of light; afterward she grows fuller and fuller, until on the 15th day she appears entirely full. This is because our eyes, positioned between her and the Sun in opposition, are able to behold as much light as she receives from him. However, the inhabitants of the higher stars see her as darkened, because the upper part facing them lacks light. 

On the 16th day, the Moon’s light begins to diminish on the side facing the west, because the Sun has outstripped her by more than half the journey. Thus, he begins to catch up to her again: just like two companions walking in a circle, where one is slow and the other fast, they are often joined together, separated, placed in opposition, and behold one another from various aspects. So, with the Sun surpassing the Moon daily by nearly four-fifths of an hour <note>In terms of celestial degrees, 4/5 of an hour equals 12 degrees, which is the average daily distance the Sun gains on the Moon.</note>, he finally catches her in 27 days and 8 hours. Consequently, twelve conjunctions are shared in a year. For this reason, the circle of the year was divided into 12 months, and the path of the sun into 12 signs named after the figures of ani-

...of the [living creatures] <note>original: *animalium*. The text fragment *lium* likely completes *animalium*, referring to the "circle of living things" or Zodiac.</note> imagined in that circle, which are *Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricornus, Aquarius, and Pisces*. And whatever **sub-deficiency** <note>As established previously, this is Campanella's term for the planets lagging behind the prime motion of the heavens.</note> the Moon suffers relative to the Sun, the Sun, Moon, and all the planets similarly suffer relative to the **fixed stars** <note>original: *fixas*. These are the stars that do not move in relation to one another, unlike the "wandering" planets.</note>. Relative to these stars, the Moon itself falls short by 13 degrees and a little more each day, but relative to the Sun it falls short by 12 degrees, because one degree of the Sun’s own sub-deficiency is subtracted from the total. Therefore, its sub-deficiency from the fixed stars is completed after 29 and a half days, at which time the motion of its **obliquity** <note>original: *obliquitatis*. This refers to the tilted path of the orbit relative to the celestial equator.</note> is also finished.

But *Mercury, the Sun, and Venus* complete their own sub-deficiency and obliquity in one solar year. *Mars* completes it in two years, *Jupiter* in 12, and *Saturn* in 30, because Saturn is the most powerful of them all in keeping pace with the fixed stars. These stars are also called "unwandering" because they are perpetually carried along the same path by rising, reaching their highest point, and setting. However, after a very long period of time, a certain obliquity among them becomes noticeable. Yet they never seem to change their distance from one another or their order, as if they were fixed together within the same sphere. 

Indeed, since they are very remote from the **hostile earth** <note>Campanella often portrays the Earth as a place of strife and "cold" matter that resists the "hot," harmonious influence of the heavens.</note>, they are not interrupted, nor do they find any occasion for battling, for deserting their order, or for diverging into different paths, as happens to the planets within their circuit. This is true unless perhaps other planets, unknown to us, circle them like Suns; regardless, their regularity is the known measure for us of the motion of the wandering stars. But because the Sun is the most well-known, is closer to us, and is the Lord of the planets, it measures all motions for us by its own movement. Therefore, the Moon takes its motion from the Sun, and the other planets take their measure and number from it as well.

Furthermore, so that variety in things might be multiplied, it pleased God that the paths of the planets be different from the path of the Sun. The Sun, by intersecting the equator with its annual obliquity, recedes from it by almost 23 and a half degrees. At the same time, the Sun's path is intersected by the travels of the other planets, which have different latitudes toward the south and the north, as the Moon clearly demonstrates. Thus, every one of them has its own **zodiac** <note>The "belt" of the sky through which a specific planet moves.</note> and its own **tropics** <note>The turning points or limits of a planet's north-south movement.</note>, which are the maximum distances on either side from the zodiac of the Sun, just as the solar tropics are the extreme points of the Sun's path furthest from the equator. They have...

The planets also have their own individual "sections" or nodes where they intersect the path of the Sun. These are commonly called the **Head and Tail of the Dragon** <note>The "Dragon" refers to the points where a planet's orbit crosses the ecliptic (the Sun's path). The "Head" is the ascending node and the "Tail" is the descending node.</note>. These nodes are most apparent in the journey of the Moon. They move forward through the signs of the Zodiac by constantly anticipating the intersections of their own equator—the lunar nodes by three minutes a day, the solar nodes by about eight "thirds" of a degree, and others by different amounts. Because of this, the **equinoxes** <note>The two times a year when day and night are equal in length.</note> are anticipated by nearly 10 seconds every year, and the **solstices** <note>The times of year when the Sun reaches its highest or lowest point in the sky at noon, marking midsummer and midwinter.</note> follow suit. Thus, the "cardinal points" <note>The points marking the start of the four seasons.</note> are no longer located in the constellations of *Aries, Libra, Cancer, and Capricorn*. In roughly 25,816 years <margin>h</margin>, the entire Zodiac could run through the whole equator, and the fated course of the world would reach its end—if these measurements did not change. But they are seen <margin>i</margin> to vary over different centuries, almost imperceptibly, and they possess an irregularity. This is because the cardinal points are not always anticipated by exactly 10 seconds, but sometimes more or less. This kind of anomaly is not always completed in 1,717 years; it is constantly changing, creating an "anomaly of the anomaly." From this, we are forced to recognize that the motion of the heavens, the measure of the life of the universe, and its various parts depend upon **God**, and not upon a "Nature" determined to act in only one way. Let us understand, then, that the world will perish by fire, especially since the Sun grows closer to the Earth every year by about ten "thirds" of a degree. For this reason, the **obliquity** <note>The tilt of the Sun’s path relative to the Earth’s equator.</note> is always shortening by about seven "fourths" of a degree, because the Sun does not need to travel far...

<meta>catchword: ...runs</meta>

*...observed the anomaly from Hipparchus to his own time. But from a single instance, one cannot conclude the same for all cases; he should have noted many more. Nor did he understand the causes of the world’s death by fire as described in the **Gospel** <note>original: *Euangelio*. Referring to the Christian New Testament prophecies about the end of the world, such as 2 Peter 3:10.</note>. Therefore, he thinks the Sun will eventually return upward and that the obliquity, which is always tightening, will eventually widen again. But it has never been observed in any century that the obliquity widened, nor that the Sun ever moved higher; rather, the angle is perpetually tightening, and the Sun is perpetually descending. Therefore, he errs through the fallacy of "begging the question" <note>original: *fallaciã petitionis principij*. A logical fallacy where the conclusion is assumed in the premises.</note> by proposing false causes for real ones—just as all mathematicians do when they propose **epicycles** and **eccentrics** <note>Complex geometric models used by ancient astronomers to explain planetary irregularities while maintaining the idea of perfect circular motion.</note> and the motion of the Earth to "save the appearances." Only God knows what these things truly are. We, however, have adapted our observations to physical principles: we have removed "violent motion," epicycles, eccentrics, the upward return of the Sun, and the motion of the Earth. We have shown that all appearances occur because of the Sun's effect on the planets, and that the equinoxes and the obliquity change because of the Sun’s descent toward the Earth to burn it. In this way, we reveal the truth of the Gospel: namely, that these phenomena and irregularities began shortly before **Eternal Wisdom** <note>A title for Jesus Christ, specifically referring to the Word of God at the Incarnation.</note> came forth for the Incarnation—the very machinery of the world being stunned by the novelty of the miracle—or perhaps after He said: "the powers of the heavens shall be shaken," and "the stars shall fall from heaven," etc. See our works on Astronomy and Metaphysics.*

Note against Copernicus: Because the latitude of the fixed stars <note>In historical astronomy, "fixed stars" are the distant stars that appear to maintain their positions relative to one another, as opposed to the "wandering" planets.</note> from the zodiac <note>The zodiac here refers to the **ecliptic**, the apparent path of the Sun across the sky.</note> always seemed the same to him, he thought that the celestial equator was inclining toward the zodiac, and that the equator is located on the Earth, while the zodiac is in the heavens.

...to run toward the poles, just as in ancient ages, since it has already prepared the earth for ignition. * Therefore, the zodiac is inclined toward the equator: this is shown by the variation in the latitude of the fixed stars relative to the zodiac, while their primeval positions remain constant among themselves. Current observations of **Antares**, **Regulus**, the **Vulture** <note>original: *Vulture*. This likely refers to the star Vega (the "Falling Vulture") or Altair (the "Flying Vulture").</note>, and the stars in the forehead of **Scorpio** already indicate this. The Sun, therefore, narrows its path and affects the earth more intensely. Because it is carried around closer to the earth, it makes the years shorter, since its rotation is narrower. The world truly grows old; it is being disposed by a most burning fever, moving gradually toward its death. However, because this approach happens irregularly, it cannot be known for certain when the "lower world" <note>The sublunary sphere, or Earthly realm.</note> will be consumed by fire. Even if it happened regularly, the exact point of approach where the Sun would burn the Earth could not be calculated. This matter God has kept hidden among his secrets. The planets follow this same pattern: for as they descend with the Sun, they shorten their obliquity <note>The angle of their orbit relative to the equator.</note>, and therefore they anticipate the equinoxes and stations similar to the solstices. And **Wisdom** <note>A personification of Divine Wisdom or the Holy Spirit.</note> said that each of them, by its own motion, measures certain beings and their various lives, which are unknown to us. We, however, measure all things by the motion of the Sun; its year serves us for the same purpose that the circulations of other celestial bodies serve for other beings in heaven and on earth.

<margin>
Since Tycho’s <note>Referring to Tycho Brahe (1546–1601), the Danish astronomer whose precise observations provided an alternative to the Copernican system.</note> observations suggest the contrary for all fixed stars—except those where the calculations of the ancients were mistaken—it follows that the zodiac is the path of the Sun, as I was saying, and that the Sun mo-
</margin>

The Sun was created in the beginning at the Equator, and likewise every planet at its own equator. But the Sun, having been made their leader, began to move from east to west and to decline continually toward the Antarctic pole. There, it liquefied much of the prepared earth and generated the **Great Ocean**, which surrounds the World and lies beneath the Southern tropic. At that point, the Sun, having moved slightly downward, was said to be at **perigee** <note>The point in an orbit where the celestial body is closest to the Earth.</note> so that it might dominate the earth. From there, it was necessary for it to return toward the Arctic, as it perceived the forces of cold to be prevailing there. Having become continually higher, it intersected the equator and established **Spring** for us. Then it traveled another 23 degrees and a little more toward our pole, and at the end of its course, having been elevated...

*...the earth, as Copernicus thinks. This argument used to trouble me greatly, and I did not believe him; but Tycho has now confirmed my conjecture. For a change in the latitude of the fixed stars is detected that matches the narrowing of the solar path, so that some stars are now closer and others more remote from the Zodiac than they were before. k Therefore, it was **Autumn** for us when the world was created; the Rabbis following **Eliezer** <note>Rabbi Eliezer ben Hyrcanus, to whom a work is attributed suggesting the world was created in the autumn month of Tishrei.</note> spoke correctly on this.*

->### CHAPTER III: ON PHYSIOLOGY###<-

...formed its apogee <note>original: *Apogeum*; the point in an orbit furthest from the Earth.</note>, and it lingered there for eight days longer than it did in the southern tropic. This occurred because the cold in the North <note>original: *Boreas*</note> had become more abundant and powerful during the Sun's absence. Thus, in the slanted path <note>The Sun's ecliptic path.</note> it took while rushing along, it transformed the earth between **Spain** and **Africa**, and between them and **America**. It turned that land into a fluid state and birthed the **Atlantic Sea**, while the southern **Ocean** followed the movement of the Sun as it moved toward the North to cleanse it. At the same time, it also created the Ocean between **China**, **Japan**, and **Quivira** <note>A legendary region of North America, often appearing on 16th-century maps in the area of the modern-day United States' Great Plains or West Coast.</note>. Remaining further away from the Northern land—which had already turned into a sticky and slippery state, though not quite into liquid—the Sun established those vast and high mountains which, stretching from east to west, divide the climates of both Hemispheres.

However, that longer delay of eight days, combined with the aid of many bright stars in our pole, caused the Sun to melt the earth beneath the pole. It established the Ocean between **Estotiland** <note>A region appearing on early maps of North America, likely corresponding to Labrador or Newfoundland.</note> and **Greenland**, and between **Nova Zembla** and the Arctic land, until it reached the borders of **Scythia** at **Arsareth** <note>A legendary land mentioned in the apocryphal book of 2 Esdras, believed by some Renaissance thinkers to be in the far north or Northeast Asia.</note>. It joined both Oceans together—namely, the Atlantic with the Ocean of Quivira and Japan—aided by the great abundance of waters flooding from the south to the north. This pattern has remained natural to the Sun from its origin: to always run its course in this way, making similar delays and gradually descending, thereby preparing the earth for the **conflagration** <note>original: *incendium*; the final destruction of the world by fire.</note> ordained by God for the end of the ages. For this reason, the Sun perpetually changes the location of its perigee <note>The point in orbit closest to the Earth.</note> and apogee from one zodiac sign to another, because a continuous variety of change is useful for different regions. Furthermore, the celestial figures are no longer in the same positions where they originally received their names; rather, where **Taurus** once was in universal space, **Aries** is now; and where Aries was, **Pisces** is now, and so on. For the <term>Active Mind</term> <note>original: *Mens Activa*; a philosophical term for the divine intelligence that governs the universe.</note> willed that the Solstices and Equinoxes should not always occur under the same fixed stars, but continually under others, so that the lower world might perpetually receive variety. The blessed Angels behold this kind of marvelous craftsmanship more clearly than men do. Similarly, the **Planets** have their own tropics, equators, nodes, and apsides <note>The highest or lowest points in an orbit.</note> when they are elevated, where they hold a **Sympathy** with other systems outside the World, and are lowered...

Nevertheless, the Sun compensates for its great power with the motion of rotation upon itself, which the other planets lack. 

Then, those planets seem to gradually become larger and faster in the following signs because they lose solar light and descend lower down. From this position, they appear larger and describe a narrower circle; therefore, they cover more of their journey, and their "lagging" is diminished. Thus, they are regularly and gradually deprived of the Sun's influence, yet they increase in light—at least to our sight—and in their own motion. This continues until the Sun reaches a distance of nearly 108 degrees from Saturn, 118 from Jupiter, and almost 133 from Mars. At this point, they repeat such a swift path in a shorter circle that at first they seem to stand still under the same fixed stars, because they are carried with a speed equal to them.

The **Moon** <note>original: *Luna*</note> finally has obtained a similar variety from the Sun, but she cannot conceive enough strength to outrun the fixed stars and be called retrograde. However, in **conjunction** <note>original: *synodo*; when the Moon and Sun are in the same celestial longitude</note> and **opposition** <note>original: *diametro*; when the Moon and Sun are on opposite sides of the Earth</note> she is raised upward because she receives direct and overflowing light, and since she is subject to the Sun, she is always raised. Others are depressed in opposition because of the narrowness of the circle and because they love to orbit the Sun. 

But the Moon, being closest to the Earth, does not descend, because she is struck by the hostile **shadow of the Earth** <note>original: *terreæ vmbra*</note>; therefore she is lifted up toward the other stars, from which she receives vigor, but not toward the Earth, by which she is harmed due to mutual proximity and her own weakness. But since the heat of the planets is excessive, and their distance is great, it frees them from the fear of the Earth during their depression. Furthermore, in squares, conjunctions, oppositions, and **trines** <note>original: *trigonis*; an astrological aspect of 120 degrees</note>, the Moon is accustomed to becoming sometimes higher, sometimes lower, and indeed slower or faster. Hence she seems to have her own **perigee** <note>original: *perigeum*; the point in an orbit closest to the Earth</note> and apogee distinct from those she obtains from the Sun, because she received this from her origin and with variety; and at certain fixed times she has a **sympathy** <note>original: *sympathiam*; a natural affinity or resonance</note> of this kind with the Beings situated above her. From this, it happens that she is raised toward them and subsequently descends. 

Here truly the **Eternal Intellect** <note>original: *Æternus Intellectus*; the divine mind or God as the architect of the universe</note> has hidden wonderful secrets, which human **Wisdom** <note>original: *Sapientia*</note> is not sufficient to reach. O, the wonders of God, who by so many lights and heats, and by multiple ways and modes—administered with natural pleasure and not by force at all—induces such variety in the university of things.

He uses heat and cold as instruments of wonderful variety. These truly are governed by love and hate, pleasure and pain.

Pleasure and pain, moreover, arise from and are tempered by Wisdom.

### CHAPTER III. ON NATURAL PHILOSOPHY

For he neither hates nor loves who does not sense the evil by which he is destroyed, nor the good by which he is preserved. Moreover, every sense comes from the **Primal Wisdom** <note>original: *prima Sapientia*; in Campanella's system, Wisdom is one of the three "Primalities" of Being</note>, and every love from the **Primal Love**: every power also comes from the **Primal Power**, which the **Triune Unity** <note>original: *Monotrias*; a term referring to the three-in-one nature of the Primalities: Power, Wisdom, and Love</note> through **Fate**, **Necessity**, and **Harmony** drives things to do, not what they might wish, but what they actually will.

<margin>
**Being** <note>original: *Ens*</note> and **Non-being** <note>original: *non Ens*</note> are the limits of finite metaphysical things. **Being** is constituted of **Power**, **Wisdom**, and **Love**. **Non-being** consists of **Impotence**, **Folly**, and **Lack of Love**. The deficiency of these finite things dissolves **being** and **not-being**. See our *Metaphysics*.
</margin>

Since indeed God *m* alone is, through Himself, infinite Being; created things, however, are not beings through themselves, but through Him, and they possess a finite entity and an infinite "nothingness." For a man is, in principle, only a man; he is not the heaven, nor a stone, nor an ox, and so on, infinitely. Therefore, he has infinite **non-beings** <note>original: *non-Entitates*; the qualities or states of being that a specific thing is NOT, which serve to define its boundaries</note> bounding and limiting his human Entity. For this reason, God—whose nature and being is every nature, and whose name is every name, and who exceeds without end all natures and names—ordained that fleeting things, born of nothing and composed of **Being** and **Non-being** in a metaphysical composition, should be measured by the motion of deficiency occurring in the oblique circle of the Sun and the planets.

<margin>The **first motion** <note>original: *motus primus*; the movement of the highest celestial sphere</note> is not the cause of the perpetuity of generation—</margin>

But **motion**, insofar as it is "nothing," is at the same time the carrier *n* of **heat** and **light**, which provide essence to our beings. It was necessary, therefore, for there to be such great variety in the heavenly bodies to induce such variety in the lower world: likewise seven wandering stars (planets); and 1021 known fixed stars, but infinite unknown ones; and their

*Physical principles are **Place**, **Matter**, **heat**, and **cold**, directed and moderated by the Metaphysicians through the first influences, namely **Necessity**, **Fate**, and **Harmony**. The **first motion** is not the cause of the perpetuity of generation and corruption, nor is the oblique motion the cause of the diversity of change; rather, it is the carrier of the Sun and Stars, and consequently of the heat and light whose operation it is. This heat is the true cause of change. The cause of perpetuity, however, is the motion in a circle by which the Sun returns to travel the same paths, insofar as the heat itself, the true agent, repeats past actions which it began from the beginning by the counsel of God. Nevertheless, it always varies until the death of the World. Irregular eccentricities show the same thing against **Aristotle**, who denied irregularity to the heaven and therefore attributed immortality to it, whereas in the present time we find the opposite of the sayings of the **Chaldeans** <note>ancient Babylonian astronomers whose long-term observations were often cited to prove or disprove the stability of the heavens</note> believed by him. Other arguments against creation found in Aristotle—namely, that there would be motion before motion and time before time—are merely logical and vain.*

# On Operation
## CHAPTER IV.
### ARTICLE I.

<margin>a. Operation is not action, nor passion as Aristotle thinks, but a habit of essence <note>original: *habitus quidditatis*; a technical term for the stable, internal state of a thing’s "whatness" or core identity</note>. Therefore, since it is preservative, it cannot <insert>be placed</insert> in the same definition as mutation (which is divided into generation, corruption, increase, decrease, and alteration, which destroy the subject). Therefore, motion is not always the "act of a being in potency" <note>Aristotle’s famous definition of motion as something moving toward a state it hasn't reached yet</note>, like mutation; but rather the act of a "being in act" <note>a being already fully realized</note>, when it is an operation.</margin>
**Operation** is an <sup>a</sup> innate act of things, by which they are preserved in their own being; therefore, it happens with pleasure in the one operating, and never ends: for if the operation fails, the very being that is activated and preserved by it also fails. <sup>b</sup> Therefore, the operation of the heaven is motion; <sup>c</sup> while that of the Earth is rest. For by rest, she is preserved; and if deprived of it, she is destroyed, just as fire is extinguished if it loses its motion. Perhaps operation is better called **Act**, lest it be seen to refer to an external work. And an Act extended into a recipient <note>original: *patiens*; literally the "patient," or the thing receiving an effect</note> is an **Action**.

<note>b. To love is a passion in reality, but an action in voice <note>grammatically</note>. To be moved in the heaven is a passion in voice, but an action in reality. To heat and to be heated are action and passion both in reality and in voice. Therefore, the Peripatetics <note>followers of Aristotle</note> are deceived when they categorize all local motion as a passive mutation. Since the motion of the heaven is an operation—which some call an "immanent action"—the Philosopher should look at things, not just words. c. Rest exists in the Earth as its vital operation; however, this does not mean the Earth is unable to participate in the good of motion because it is "dead," as Aristotle teaches. On the contrary, motion would be an evil for it, because the Earth is contrary to the heaven, not loving its entity <note>meaning the Earth's nature seeks to maintain its identity through stillness rather than movement</note>.</note>

# On Action and Passion.
### ARTICLE II.

<margin>a. The Peripatetic definition, that Action is the efficacy by which <insert>we are said to act</insert></margin>
**Action** is <sup>a</sup> the pouring out of the likeness of the agent into the recipient <note>original: *patiens*</note>, which must therefore be contrary or different from it. For if it is entirely similar, it does not suffer from it; since to act is a certain making similar...

<note>...by which we are said to act upon a subject, etc., is a grammatical delusion explaining nothing. For in this way we could define everything: the Soul is that by which we are said to be animated; light is that by which we are luminous; cold is that by which we are cold, etc.</note>

<summary>Campanella defines "Operation" as the internal, preservative activity of a being—such as motion for the heavens and rest for the Earth—contrasting it with external "Action." He critiques Aristotelian physics for failing to distinguish between grammatical terms and the actual nature of physical existence.</summary>

# ON PHYSIOLOGICAL MATTERS. CHAPTER IV. 31

...to assimilate to itself that which is dissimilar. For if it is already similar, it has already been assimilated; therefore, the action, which is the process of assimilation itself, ceases. The stars do not act upon other stars, but upon the earth; and every contrary acts upon its contrary insofar as it is contrary or different in form. Therefore, every natural action involves labor, and every agent desires the end of its action: if that end is achieved with victory, it is pleasant, because the agent is multiplied and made safe by the destruction of its contrary, and it returns to its own free operation. For this reason, all fires generated on the earth return to the heavens as victors, so that there they may be joined and moved with their own kind with joy. But if the action results in loss, it is painful for the opposite reasons.

**Passion** <term>Passion: From the Latin *passio*, meaning "to undergo" or "to be acted upon." In this context, it refers to the state of receiving an influence from an external source.</term> is therefore the reception of an external likeness, whether natural—such as when the earth, having been heated, becomes hot, similar to the heaven that heats it; or as a man born is similar to the one who generated him—or mental, as this writing is similar to the Wisdom of my mind, and this house is similar to the carpenter's idea. 

<margin>God is a free agent, not a natural or necessary one, although He possesses the essence of both types of agent in an eminent way <note>original: *eminenter*; a philosophical term meaning that God possesses qualities in a higher, more perfect way than created things do</note>, as good theologians teach.</margin> 

The World, indeed, is similar to the Divine Idea, although God in Himself contains mental and natural likeness in a certain maximal and divine unity from which they flow. From this it is recognized that just as this writing is not like the pen—the instrumental agent—but like me, Tommaso Campanella, the principal agent through my knowledge, which depends on the First Wisdom; so also the World is not like heat or cold (which are merely God’s instruments), but like the Divine Idea. 

Yet it is also true in part, and in its parts, that the world is similar to the instruments through which the divine art is impressed upon things, and upon their whole universe with wonderful craftsmanship: just as this writing is also similar to the thinness of the pen and the color of the ink in its shape, but similar to my mind in its meaning and doctrine.

<meta>This page continues Chapter IV of Campanella’s Physiologica. It builds on the previous discussion of "Action" and "Passion" by classifying the various ways physical things change and interact. The catchword on the previous page was "ordo" (order).</meta>

# BROTHER TOMMASO CAMPANELLA

**Change** <term>Change: Latin *mutatio*</term> is either of the whole being—and this is called the **destruction** <term>destruction: Latin *corruptio*, the ceasing of a previous state of being</term> of the preceding state, and the **generation** <term>generation: Latin *generatio*, the beginning of a new state of being</term> of the following; or it is of the parts of the material temperament, and this is called the **increase** <term>increase: Latin *augmentum*</term> of the thing to which they are added, and the **decrease** <term>decrease: Latin *decrementum*</term> of the thing from which they are taken. Or it is a slight change and merely a disposition toward these transformations, a certain change not of the Being itself, but of its internal or external conditions; and this is called **alteration** <term>alteration: Latin *alteratio*</term>, just as when a silkworm becomes a moth <note>original: *pyrausta*, a Greek term for a moth that seeks the flame</note>, or a crawling ant becomes a winged one, or an open palm becomes a fist.

<margin>I wish to include **Transformation**, which has been omitted by other philosophers, because it concerns material aspects relative to the subject, not ideal forms, nor active ones. For the "idea" of a triangle does not become the "idea" of a quadrangle, nor does heat become cold; rather, this waxy triangle becomes this waxy quadrangle, since it is not annihilated. Philosophers did not omit Division and Union, except for Aristotle; but it is clear that they are necessary for the Physiologist <note>a student of the natural world</note>.</margin>

a. I also think that transformation occurs when a triangle is expanded into a circle: for it is not indeed annihilated, and therefore every passive form and material boundary is transformed, but not the active ones: for heat cannot become cold, but a straight line can become a circle.

**Division** and **union** also occur in Nature, followed by scattering, gathering, thinning <term>thinning: Latin *rarefactio*</term>, and thickening <term>thickening: Latin *condensatio*</term>, which are types of change in the subject, not in its quantity or quality. Likewise, there is **change of color**, as when black comes from white; for when it simply becomes whiter, that is an Alteration, which does not change the type of color, but only its quality. We also say that one **Act** changes into another act, such as motion into rest, but the acceleration of motion is an alteration of its quality. Quality, however, exists in every category of being. There are also changes in the other relative Categories, but they follow from the absolute ones. From this, one may recognize that the violent local motion of a stone <note>such as when a stone is thrown upward against its natural gravity</note> is not an operation <note>an internal act of being</note>, but a passion <note>something the stone undergoes or suffers from an outside force</note>. But when motion occurs for the convenience of the agent or the receiver together—as when a sailor moves a ship, or the spirit moves the body—even though the primary benefit belongs to the mover itself, it is always called **carrying** or **transporting**.

Observing these things as a mixture of action and passion, we shall understand how the two elements act against one another, and how compound bodies <term>compound bodies: Latin *elementata*, things made of the elements</term> are formed. They do this by drawing together the weakened and restrained conditions of the elements, as well as their manner of acting and operating; just as they themselves learned from God when they were created from nothing; and at the same time, they receive the **Idea of the First Wisdom**.

<summary>Campanella defines and categorizes the different types of physical change—such as generation, alteration, and his proposed "transformation"—explaining how matter takes on new shapes and qualities without being destroyed. He concludes by linking these physical processes to the divine "Idea" implanted in nature by God at the moment of creation.</summary>

<header>PHYSIOLOGICAL STUDIES, CHAPTER IV.</header>

## The order of communication of the primary opposing agents into the passive causes.

### ARTICLE IV.

Heat, therefore, which is the celestial active cause, first and by its own nature warms; that is, it impresses and communicates itself into the foreign terrestrial element <note>In Campanella's system, Heat is the active, living principle of the Heavens, while Earth/Cold is the passive, "foreign" principle it acts upon</note>, because it has received the power of diffusion from the First Power <note>The "First Power" refers to the primordial power of God, one of Campanella's three "Primalities": Power, Wisdom, and Love</note>. Therefore, it also destroys cold by accident at the same time. Secondly, by entering the mass, it thins and rarefies it. Thirdly, if it is powerful enough, it moves the thinned portion upward. Afterward, however, <margin>a Aristotle incorrectly denies whiteness to air and water, and denies all heat to the elements, teaching that colored beings are created from those without color.</margin> it whitens and illuminates, as clouds raised by strong heat demonstrate—which, despite the heat, appear black initially. But if the heat is mild, or even strong but enclosed so that it cannot escape, it first whitens and afterward moves the overcome mass. Yet because it is blunted by cold while it acts—[the order of cold's action is: first to chill, second to condense, third to immobilize, fourth to blacken]—heat itself is diminished, as are its properties, and it becomes impure; and thus it establishes things that are diminished and not purely celestial.

*...[continuing from the margin above] colored beings, which is impossible. Elsewhere, however, he [Aristotle] says fire is red (as in Book 1 of the Meteorology <note>Aristotle's treatise on natural phenomena</note>); elsewhere white (as in the third book); elsewhere (as in the second) that air whitens the sight and is white. But in the book On Colors, he asserts that fire and the Sun are yellow, while air, water, and earth are white. This is false, for yellowness is created by the mixture of smoke and the whiteness of fire, as he himself teaches in his work on the Rainbow. Indeed, no one would deny that the earth is black and opaque. The example he brings of white ash being "pure earth" is deceptive. For ash is earth conquered by fire and whitened by it. He also mistakenly thinks that blackness comes from excessive humidity; if so, water and air, being the most humid, would be black, yet they are white.*

<meta>This page continues the investigation into the physical properties of matter. While the previous page focused on how heat and matter produce colors, this page details the specific stages of transformation as matter is "dissolved" by heat, moving from solid states to invisible vapors. It concludes by linking these physical states to Campanella’s core metaphysical theory of the "Primalities"—Power, Wisdom, and Love.</meta>

### CHAPTER V OF PHYSICAL MATTERS

<margin>a Flour is a dry being broken into minute fragments.</margin>
<margin>b Dryness follows the density and constriction of matter; therefore, fire is not inherently dry, since it is rare (thin). However, fire "dries" accidentally by uncovering the dryness mixed with humidity, which it draws out and carries with it to its kindred heaven. Humidity follows the rarefaction and expansion of matter; therefore, fire is "humid"—that is, thin and rare—but not "wet" like water, which signifies a thick and imperfect humidity.</margin>

The first stage of transformation is called **stickiness** <note>original: *lentor*, referring to a tough, pliable, or "slow" state of matter</note>. Then, as the heat dissolves it further and arranges it in its own way, it turns into **softness**, which yields more easily to the touch because it has unfolded its parts further; hence, these parts can be pressed into themselves, which is what it means to "yield." Then it turns into **viscosity**, which is a density that resists being thinned, or a liquid that resists being thickened—just as a watery liquid mixed with <margin>a</margin> dry flour demonstrates. Then, as the heat acts further, it is dissolved into **slipperiness** <note>original: *lubricositas*</note>, which is a flowing and running viscosity. Then it becomes a **liquid**, which flows even more; then into **vapor** or **smoke**, which, having lost its bulk, is lifted upward. Finally, it is driven into an **invisible thinness**, which contains fewer parts in a larger space—just as, conversely, a **dense** object contains more parts in a narrower space. **Lightness**, **subtlety**, and **humidity** immediately follow this thinness (or "rarity"), just as **heaviness**, **thickness**, and <margin>b</margin> **dryness** follow density. And all "secondary matters" <note>Created physical substances as opposed to "prime matter"</note> possess some of these temperaments as their **substantial form**, which is the final degree of the arrangement and order of particles, established together with their active powers, and received at the end of their generation.

<margin>c The name "form" properly belongs to the external shape; but it is transferred here to the internal temperament of a created thing, shaped at its own specific degree, and to the Idea of the creator.</margin>

Just as <margin>c</margin> the final degree of thinness of a liquid dissolved by heat becomes the "form" of **air** when it passes into that state (carrying with it that degree of heat which remains and is brought along), so too this kind of final habit—the goal of generation—is a degree of participation in the **eternal Idea**. From this, the **power** of being in such a way, the **wisdom** of preserving oneself, and the **love** of living in such a way, are drawn together into that specific state and manner. And the unity of these **Primalities** <note>Campanella’s signature metaphysical doctrine: *Potentia* (Power), *Sapientia* (Wisdom), and *Amor* (Love) are the three fundamental principles of all being.</note> is implanted in **Nature**, which is **Divine Art**.

## *On the differences between the actions of mild and strong heat*

### ARTICLE III.

**F**ar more degrees of transformation exist, composed by the logic we have mentioned, which are maintained by moderate heat—as is clearly seen in wax. However, strong heat, as soon as it has unfolded the matter, makes it thin and causes it to evaporate, so that the aforementioned degrees are not easily discerned, even though they occur. 

And if the matter is composed of similar parts—namely, parts that are all equally soft or equally liquid—then while the heat evaporates, no portion of it remains, as is shown by "water of life" <note>original: *aqua vitæ*; a term for distilled spirits or brandy, which evaporates completely</note> and a very few other substances. 

But if the matter consists of dissimilar parts—that is, thick, thin, slippery, and viscous parts all together, which is the nature of almost all our worldly Entities due to the various actions they receive from the Sun and Stars in manifold movements, ways, and times—a variety occurs, such that the matter is hardened by the strong action of the heat. For the heat turns the less hard and less resistant portions into thinness, into its own substance, and carries them upward; but the denser parts become and are left harder, just as is seen in mud placed near a fire. For when the mud is deprived of the softer watery part, in which the hard earthy part lay hidden, that hardness is revealed as the water evaporates. 

Therefore, heat hardens and thickens "by accident" <note>original: *per accidens*; an Aristotelian term meaning an indirect or unintended effect</note> and unintentionally; that is, it reveals the hardness and density already present. In the same way, intense heat seems to generate blackness while it uncovers it, by drawing out the thinned and whitened parts (which it has refined) upward, and not permitting them to remain to arrange the thick parts left behind toward whiteness and thinness. This is in contrast to what mild heats are accustomed to do; because mild heats are not strong enough to draw out those portions, they remain with them within the mass and more perfectly "cook" <term>coctio: the process of refining or maturing matter through heat</term> the earth. At the same time, from both the thick and the thin parts, they constitute more of our earthly beings. This is what springtime teaches us: it is lukewarm and suitable for generation <note>the creation of new life</note>, the opposite of burning summer and the destruction...

# On the dispositions of secondary matter in the act of generation, designated and adapted for each secondary being.

### ARTICLE IV.

<margin>
a. Concerning the liquid matter of these things.
</margin>
**A**ll beings between Heaven and Earth are generated from these mixed dispositions. Indeed, if <margin>a</margin> heat liquefies Earth, it generates water or other liquids according to the variety of the heat. For strong heat produces thick and impure liquids from dense and dissimilar <note>original: *dissimilari*; referring to heterogeneous matter made of different types of particles</note> earth; but from similar <note>original: *similari*; homogeneous matter</note> and dense earth, it produces thick and pure ones. From soft and similar earth, it draws out thin and pure liquids; but from soft and dissimilar earth, it draws impure and thin ones. Gentle heat, however, whether the matter be thick or loose, always generates purer liquids—though more dense from the former and less dense from the latter. From these liquids, and from slipperiness and stickiness, stones and metals are formed.

<margin>
b. Concerning vapor as the matter of things.
</margin>
If heat turns earth into <margin>b</margin> vapor, it generates winds, rains, comets, and other beings that occur in the air according to their designated matter. For strong heat draws thick, impure vapors from dense, dissimilar matter; but pure ones from similar matter. Yet gentle heat draws thin and pure vapors from dense matter; and from soft matter, it draws thick and pure ones (sometimes more, sometimes less, if they are similar). When it hardens and binds them together, it gives birth to stones.

<margin>
c. Concerning the matter of plants.
</margin>
If it generates <margin>c</margin> a thick smoke which, emerging clothed in viscosity and stickiness, cannot separate itself from Mother Earth <note>original: *matre tellure*</note>, it turns into a plant as the spiritual smoke <note>In early modern science, "spirits" or "spiritual smoke" referred to the volatile, active gases thought to drive growth and life.</note> tries to lift itself upward. Thus, the portion that has left the earth's surface and is exposed to the outside hardens; the interior portion, however, grows upward, drawn by heat, and simultaneously grows downward from a desire to suck up terrestrial liquid similar to itself, from which it draws its origin and nourishment.
